a: The ERD entity stencil's attribute fields put the name in `label` and the type/key in `value`, the reverse of the ER reader and writer
The UML interface stencil spells its stereotype `«interface»`, which the class writer does not read as an annotation, so it exports as a class named "«interface»" with "Interface" as an attribute
The abstract-class stencil marks abstraction only with italics, which the class writer drops without a warning
The mind map's subtopic stencil uses `stadium`, which the mind map writer has no brackets for, so every placed subtopic exports plain with a warning
`expectStencilsBuild` checks each row's width against text measured in the default style, not the row's own bold or font size
`expectStencilsBuild` leaves `console.warn` mocked when any assertion inside it fails
b: The UML interface stencil spells its stereotype `«interface»`, which the class writer and reader don't recognize
The ERD entity stencil's field rows put the attribute name where the ER reader and writer keep its type
The abstract-class stencil marks abstractness only as italic, which the class writer drops without a warning
The mind-map subtopic and note stencils use outlines the mindMap type's Mermaid notation can't write
The BPMN end event differs from a start event only by stroke width, so draw.io export writes it as a start event
`expectStencilsBuild` checks row width against the text measured unstyled, so a bold or large row that overflows passes
`expectStencilsBuild` counts only label and field rows, but header rows also become text nodes
`expectStencilsBuild` leaves its `console.warn` spy installed when an assertion fails
